It happens gradually

Small gaps become real business risks.

Most businesses do not set out with disorganised IT. They grow, solve the next problem quickly and add technology as they need it. Eventually, everyday work becomes harder to manage, less secure and much more difficult to hand over.

Personal email is doing business work

Customer conversations, invoices and company logins live in personal inboxes rather than an account the business controls.

Nobody is quite sure who owns what

The domain, website, email, social accounts or cloud files may be registered to a former employee, a freelancer or an old personal account.

Passwords are scattered

Important logins are shared in messages, saved in browsers or known by only one person.

Files have grown wherever there was space

Documents are split between laptops, USB drives, personal cloud storage and old accounts, with no obvious backup or handover plan.

Technology has been added bit by bit

Each tool may have solved an immediate problem, but together they are difficult to manage, secure and support.

A staff change would create a scramble

When someone leaves, it is not clear what access they have, what needs transferring or how the business keeps working.

The review

A clear picture of where you are now.

Our free Small Business Technology Review is a practical conversation about the technology your business relies on. There is no scare tactic or jargon-heavy report — just a useful view of what is working, what is exposed and what would make the biggest difference.

Business email & Microsoft 365

A professional email setup, clear ownership and the right tools for communication and collaboration.

Domains, DNS & website access

Who owns the important accounts, how they are secured and whether you can make changes when you need to.

Passwords, MFA & access

A safer, manageable way to protect sign-ins and control who can reach company systems.

Files, backups & recovery

Where business information lives, how it is shared and what happens if a device is lost or fails.

Devices & day-to-day support

Whether laptops, phones and other equipment are set up consistently and ready for the people using them.

Your practical next steps

A prioritised, plain-English outline of what to fix first, what can wait and where OS Technology can help.

How it works

Three straightforward steps.

01

Tell us how things work today

We start with your people, the systems you use and any worries already on your mind. You do not need to prepare a technical inventory.

02

We map the important pieces

Together, we look at ownership, access, security and how the essentials fit together — from email and files to devices and your website.

03

You get sensible priorities

We explain what should be addressed first, what can be planned for later and how to make the setup easier to run going forward.

What good looks like

One company. One point of contact. A proper setup.

The aim is not to make your business more complicated. It is to make the technology behind it clear, owned by the business and ready to support the next stage of growth.
